about: Synthetic simulation output; design aid only, no evidence credit (sim/README.md, evidence gate).

proposal.rationale: Preliminary. Ankle 1.5 m g L_foot at full supply (0.6 m g L_foot at the 0.4 load-holding threshold) and knee 26.5 kN m, as adopted (DQ-024, DQ-026), with CL-05 standing on a knee bent 0.3 rad (DQ-027) instead of the 1.018 rad it was drawn with. That deep stance puts the knee 0.46 m behind the line of the ground force, so one leg needs about 25 kN m at the knee and the knee must still give it at the 0.4 load-holding threshold: in that stance the knee needs 62.5 kN m to clear the grid (knee sweep). Straightening the stance shortens that moment arm: the adopted knee clears the grid from 0.4 rad and both grids from 0.35 to 0.25 rad, and fails again at 0.2 rad, where the nearly straight knee has no travel left to absorb the load (posture sweep); 0.3 rad is the middle of that band, and there every ankle value in the sweep clears (ankle sweep). The straighter stance raised the hips by 0.23 m (CL-05 redrawn, cad/metrics.json). Joint torque is taken to fall in proportion to supply (level-2 assumption, as A4 at level 1).

title: Ankle and knee torque against supply loss on a slope
